domain_setting: A small modern office where colleagues plan work, communicate, negotiate, follow procedures, estimate costs, and solve ordinary commercial problems.
visual_thesis: Use workplace props and distinct human actions to make each idiom's intended meaning clear without printed words, numbers, logos, or literal captions.
recurring_scale_anchors: Blank proposal sheets and folders signal workplace planning without legible writing.
A shared desk or meeting table grounds scenes in a small office.
Use varied coworkers in blue, sage, and warm neutral clothing; avoid logos and readable text.
When a sports metaphor is required, include a small office cue such as a folder or colleague so the business sense stays primary.

reviewed_existing_art.exact_term_scan: No same-slug SVG candidates were found in the authored vocabulary art or mapped course art for any of these 25 terms.
reviewed_existing_art.decision: Author all 25 cards in business context; there is no existing illustration to keep for these exact terms.

polysemy_resolution_table.ahead of the game: Prepared or more advanced than others in a business task, not physically ahead in a sports match.
polysemy_resolution_table.back to square one: A failed work plan must restart from its beginning; use a planning board, not a literal game board.
polysemy_resolution_table.business as usual: Ordinary commercial work continues routinely despite a minor disruption.
polysemy_resolution_table.change of pace: A welcome change from the usual work rhythm or task.
polysemy_resolution_table.game plan: A deliberate workplace strategy for reaching a goal, not necessarily a sports play.
polysemy_resolution_table.get down to business: Begin serious practical work after preparation or small talk.
polysemy_resolution_table.get the ball rolling: Start a project or process and prompt others to join.
polysemy_resolution_table.raise the bar: Set a higher standard or level of performance.
polysemy_resolution_table.think outside the box: Find an unconventional but useful workplace solution.
polysemy_resolution_table.ball is in your court: Responsibility to make the next decision or take the next action has passed to a colleague.
polysemy_resolution_table.circle back: Return to a colleague or topic later to continue a work discussion.
polysemy_resolution_table.in a nutshell: A complicated business proposal reduced to its concise main idea.
polysemy_resolution_table.on the same page: Colleagues share the same understanding of a plan.
polysemy_resolution_table.take it offline: Move a side discussion out of a large online meeting into a smaller private conversation.
polysemy_resolution_table.touch base: Make brief contact with a colleague to exchange a status update.
polysemy_resolution_table.win-win: An agreement gives a useful benefit to both parties.
polysemy_resolution_table.ballpark figure: A rough business estimate, not a baseball player's statistics or a final exact price.
polysemy_resolution_table.clinch the deal: Secure a commercial agreement through a final handshake or sealed blank contract.
polysemy_resolution_table.corner the market: One seller gains dominant control of a product market, depicted as occupying its key sales area.
polysemy_resolution_table.do something by the book: Follow established rules or procedures in a work task.
polysemy_resolution_table.in the red: A business has financial losses, shown by a falling chart and reduced funds.
polysemy_resolution_table.move the goalposts: Unfairly change the requirements after a worker has nearly met the original target.
polysemy_resolution_table.red tape: Excessive bureaucracy delays routine business paperwork.
polysemy_resolution_table.throw money down the drain: Waste a business budget on an ineffective purchase or project.
polysemy_resolution_table.business: Commercial work, trade, or an enterprise; not a particular company name or business meeting.

entries.ahead of the game: A prepared coworker finishes a key planning task while others are still organizing their papers.
entries.back to square one: A rejected project route sends a marker back to the first starting square on a work-planning board.
entries.business as usual: A calm clerk continues an ordinary customer transaction at a desk despite a small overturned cup nearby.
entries.change of pace: A coworker leaves repetitive desk sorting to take a short, relaxed walk and return refreshed.
entries.game plan: Two coworkers arrange a few connected steps on a planning board leading to a business goal.
entries.get down to business: A team sets aside refreshments, opens blank folders, and begins focused work at a meeting table.
entries.get the ball rolling: A colleague pushes a blue ball toward a line of project blocks to start them moving.
entries.raise the bar: A team lifts a visible performance threshold higher while a worker reaches toward it.
entries.think outside the box: A colleague steps out of an open cardboard box and presents an unexpected useful solution.
entries.ball is in your court: Two coworkers face one another across a small court-like floor mark; the ball rests beside the colleague who must decide next.
entries.circle back: A colleague follows a curved route back toward a teammate and a shared work folder.
entries.in a nutshell: A small blank proposal card fits inside an opened nutshell, representing the compact main idea.
entries.on the same page: Two coworkers lean over and point to one shared blank planning sheet.
entries.take it offline: Two colleagues step aside to talk with a closed laptop while the larger remote meeting continues faintly on a screen.
entries.touch base: A colleague briefly checks in and exchanges a folder at the office doorway.
entries.win-win: Two business partners complete an agreement and each receives an equally useful parcel.
entries.ballpark figure: A broad shaded range on a blank business chart sits beside a small baseball field motif, clearly an estimate rather than an exact amount.
entries.clinch the deal: Two partners seal a successful agreement with a decisive handshake over a closed blank contract folder.
entries.corner the market: A single seller's full product stall occupies the corner of a simple market row while nearby competing stands are vacant.
entries.do something by the book: An office worker follows the illustrated steps in an open blank procedure manual, marking each step with a check.
